text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: INC-2025-1012 declared (eu-west): increased fallback selections + customer reports of model switching. Owner: Monica Patel.

Monica Patel: Seeing route_fallback_selected jump from ~0.2% to ~22% in eu-west. Primary pool looks green though.

Ethan Park: If primary is healthy, this smells like policy eval bug or cache. Any router config changes today?

Ava Chen: There was a policy tweak this morning to make queue-depth protection more aggressive in eu-west. Might be overfiring.

Rishi Malhotra: Can you paste the diff? Also check whether the fallback check runs before model pinning preference.

Ava Chen: Diff summary: changed queue_depth_p95 window from 5m to 30s and lowered threshold. Also added a condition on scheduler backlog that might be noisy.

Monica Patel: OK rolling back eu-west routing ruleset to previous revision now.

Incident Bot: Deploy Bot: rollback initiated for routing-policy eu-west (rev 2025-10-11.3).

Chloe Martin: Support side: Acme, Pinecone AI, and a self-serve customer all saying responses look different. They mention different model IDs in headers.

Ethan Park: After rollback, fallback rate dropped but still ~6%. Might be policy cache not refreshing.

Monica Patel: Agree. Flushing policy eval cache on router nodes in eu-west.

Incident Bot: Runbook step executed: router policy cache flush (eu-west).

Ava Chen: Also adding a temporary guard: if strict pin header present AND primary capacity healthy, do not evaluate fallback.

Rishi Malhotra: :thumbsup: Please ensure we capture this in postmortem and add an invariant test.

Monica Patel: Metrics now: fallback rate back to 0.3% baseline. Customer reports should subside. Keeping incident open 30m to confirm.

Chloe Martin: Customer just confirmed model id stable again. Will update SUP-4187.

Incident Bot: INC-2025-1012 resolved.
